tier_reason: Tier stays C (indirect pg_jitter evidence). Enricher found the Wide1K rows behind the headline compile ratio have sljit compiling almost nothing under the old deform cap, so the compile-time comparison is restated without them.

corrections.claimed_speedup: pg_jitter BENCHMARKS_v18.md (PostgreSQL 18, ARM64 M1 Pro): execution SUM_int 68.090 vs llvmjit 42.401 ms and GroupBy_5agg 149.033 vs 99.530 ms (sljit slower than llvmjit at run time; slower than the interpreter on 27 of 108 queries, minimum 0.81x on LIKE_3wild). Compile time 0.04-0.46 ms vs llvmjit 17-2043 ms: 220-1,040x, median about 480x without the Wide1K rows (derived from page data); the Wide1K rows (21,000-29,000x) have sljit compiling almost nothing under pg_jitter 0.3.0's deform cap and are not comparable.
corrections.caveats: Indirect evidence: a patched vladich/sljit fork (upstream as of February 2026 plus 2 SIMD commits) as a pg_jitter backend, not the library alone; compiler and flags unstated, ARM64 only on a single M1 Pro, and the harness forces LLVM inlining and optimization at cost 0. The Wide1K rows reflect the old deform cap that current pg_jitter source calls incorrect. pg_jitter_sljit.c adds emission time to both generation_counter and emission_counter, so EXPLAIN totals double-count it. Upstream defaults SLJIT_DEBUG=1 and SLJIT_VERBOSE=1; open crash and miscompile issues #376, #366, #271.

tier_reason: Tier stays B (independent jedisct1 2021 shootout). Enricher recounted the 59 macOS logs: the total-time lead is dominated by pwhash_scrypt and the per-test geomeans are much smaller than the total-time ratios.

tier_reason: Tier stays A (dasProfile code, flags and CPU published). Enricher found the Lua kernels are not written like for like, so the headline ratios over Lua are restated with the independent sashi0034 figure and the parity fib row.

corrections.claimed_speedup: borisbat/dasProfile (Linux, Ryzen 7 PRO 8700GE, Clang 19): the DAS interpreter beats Lua 5.5.1 and QuickJS on all 16 kernels, but the largest gaps (sha256 27x, mandelbrot 32x, particles 41x over Lua) come from Lua kernels written differently (bit operations through vararg select() wrappers, metatable Complex tables, 11 passes vs 10); the like-for-like recursive fib is parity (0.048174 vs 0.048747 s), and the independent sashi0034/script-language-benchmark suite puts the DAS advantage over Lua at about 2.5x (derived from page data). QuickJS: sha256 0.002510 vs 0.021312 s, mandelbrot 0.001791 vs 0.006346 s, sort 0.015450 vs 0.037570 s.
corrections.caveats: dasProfile is a first-party suite by the Daslang lead with no licence; DAS SDK flags are not in the bench repo, LuaJIT -joff and Mono --interpreter win some kernels, the dictionary cell varies by about 25%, and the Lua kernels are not like for like (the DAS sha256 also loads raw words without byteswap and is right only because the input is all '.'). Open crash issues #4110, #3734, #4101.

tier_reason: Tier stays B. Enricher found the suite's gcc-15 build disables toywasm's musttail dispatch and LTO, and the Wasmtime baseline lacks parallel compilation, so the execution and startup ratios are both distorted; the startup win itself holds.

corrections.caveats: Startup-only win: execution is x318.96 against WAMR's x17.07 in the wasmi-benchmarks suite, but that suite builds toywasm with gcc-15 (platform.h gates musttail on __clang__, so dispatch falls back to return-to-loop and the C code gets no LTO), which likely explains 18.7x slower than WAMR on the EPYC against about 8.7x on the M2 Pro and 3.5x vs wasm3 in the author's clang run. The Wasmtime baseline is built default-features=false without parallel compilation, so the x1634 startup ratio is inflated (the author's own run: 40.94 s user vs 4.87 s real). The author's startup.csv has the WAMR classic interpreter at 0.19 s against toywasm's 0.18 s. Run through a wrapper written by the Wasmi author with no compiler versions. UBSan issue #362, OOM trap inconsistency #258.

tier_reason: Tier stays C (first-party README). Enricher found the benchmark scripts favour Mobius (typed fib parameters, preallocation inside the timer, CPU time for Lua against wall clock for the others, native-tuned build) and that the geomean is 0.93x of Lua.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README totals 373.9 ms vs Lua 443.3 ms vs CPython 1424.8 ms are whole-script times including untimed setup; per-row geomean is 0.93x of Lua's time and 0.47x of CPython's (about 2.1x faster than CPython, not 3.8x; derived from page data). The committed benchmark_summary_latest.json (2026-07-12) has Mobius 1.3x slower than Lua.
corrections.caveats: Benchmark scripts favour Mobius: fib is annotated 'n: int64): int64' despite a comment saying it is unannotated, the mixed workload preallocates with array_create(n) inside the timer while Lua and Python start empty, Lua is timed with os.clock (CPU time) against wall clock for the others, and Mobius is built -march=native -flto against Lua and CPython from PATH; superinstructions such as AGET_ADD_CHECK match the loop shapes. Hardware, Lua and CPython versions unstated; the README Lua win has no committed raw results; 3 stars.
